# spotlight_runner_trust (Resource)

A workload whose platform-issued tokens let a `spotlight-host` claim work, as a Kubernetes service account's do: a host there holds no Spotlight token and claims through the trust with its workload token, given `SPOTLIGHT_TRUST=<trust id>` and `SPOTLIGHT_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE=<projected token path>`. Writing runner trusts needs a token granted the `runners` scope. Import it as `<workspace id>/<key>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "spotlight_runner_trust" "production_cluster" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  key          = "production-cluster"
  issuer       = "https://oidc.eks.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLE"
  subject      = "system:serviceaccount:spotlight:runner"
  labels       = ["gpu"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `issuer` (String) The https URL the platform signs its workloads' tokens as; its keys are found through OIDC discovery.
- `key` (String) Names the trust, as in `production-cluster`. It is fixed for the runner trust's life, so changing it replaces the runner trust.
- `subject` (String) The workload a token must be issued to, exactly, as in `system:serviceaccount:spotlight:runner`.
- `workspace_id` (String) The workspace the runner trust belongs to. Changing it replaces the runner trust.

### Optional

- `audience` (String) The audience a token must be issued for.
- `labels` (Set of String) What a line or station may name in `runners` to place its work on the runners claimed through here, as in `gpu`.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `production-cluster`.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the runner trust is created, and never changed.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the runner trust; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_runner_trust.production_cluster
  identity = {
    id = "3f8a1c2e-6b4d-4e7a-9c1f-0d2b5e8a7c63"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the runner trust when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_runner_trust.production_cluster
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/production-cluster"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a runner trust with the id of its workspace and its key.
terraform import spotlight_runner_trust.production_cluster 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/production-cluster
```
